mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the FEDFUNDS rate above 4% signals a tightening cycle that increases discount rates, lowering the present value of future equity cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: In a tightening regime, 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) or FEDFUNDS declines back below 4% within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in PAYEMS accompanied by a concurrent decline in UNRATE suggests a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In 30% of similar labor strength events, 20-day forward returns fail to exceed baseline by more than 1% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in HOUST above 500 indicates growing industrial demand, which typically precedes corporate investment and equity market expansion, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 40 consecutive months of HOUST > 500, 20-day forward returns average no more than 0.5% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in INDPRO above 96 coincides with reduced inflation pressures, signaling a supply-side easing that lowers real interest rates and supports equity valuations, yielding positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses above 96 while CPIAUCSL shows flattening momentum
failure_condition: In 5 consecutive supply easing episodes, 60-day returns are negative or flat (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains persistently below 1% for three consecutive months, it indicates a accommodative stance that lowers real rates and encourages risk-taking, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS stays below 1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 20 such periods, 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in UNRATE below 5% suggests weaker wage growth, raising uncertainty about consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which tends to depress S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In 60% of UNRATE < 5% episodes, 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of accelerating GDPC1 growth above 10% indicate robust business demand that outpaces supply, prompting market participants to price in higher future earnings and equity valuations, producing positive 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 15 such demand spikes, 60-day returns fail to beat the mean by 2% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS falls below 300 million for two consecutive months while UNRATE remains above 6%, it indicates weak demand and tight supply conditions that suppress equity risk premia, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: In 10 such supply tightness episodes, 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1).
